Definition: a cordon, (adverbially) or (as a) military barrier
BiblicalUsage: The word names a cordon, a military barrier or guard, and it appears once, in the guarding of the young king Joash: a third part of the guard stood at the gate behind the guard, so they would keep the watch of the house and the king would not be broken in upon.
TheologicalSignificance: I hold that the guard around Joash is the picture of God's own watch over His anointed, and no usurper breaks through it.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
